title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1
summary: Anthropic released two new models, Claude Fable 5.

title: OpenAI launches Astra, a product built for legal work
summary: OpenAI announced Astra for Law, a version of its technology aimed specifically at legal professionals.

title: Waymo's driverless taxis are going to Singapore
summary: Waymo announced it is bringing its self-driving service to Singapore, its first move into Asia.

title: A marketing team put its event process into code — and automated it
summary: A GitHub marketer wrote up how their APAC team turned event planning and follow-up into automated workflows, on the argument that if you can write down how you do your work, you can automate it.

title: A 27-billion-parameter model squeezed into a ninth of the space
summary: Researchers released Bonsai 2 27B, a compressed model they say keeps almost all of the original's quality in a footprint nine times smaller.

title: GitHub rewrote the Copilot runtime in Rust — 800,000 lines of it
summary: GitHub moved the runtime behind Copilot to Rust, ending up with roughly 800,000 lines of production code, and used Copilot itself to do much of the porting.

title: Your AI agent passed the test. Will it pass it again?
summary: IBM researchers argue that almost nobody reports the metric that matters most for agents: consistency.

title: Google's Gemini was reportedly used to hack three companies
summary: According to a Wall Street Journal report relayed by Reuters, Google's Gemini model was used to break into three companies — described as the first known case of Google's AI being turned on real targets rather than test systems.

title: Alibaba released a free medical AI that screens for cancer and ~150 other conditions
summary: Alibaba open-sourced a medical model it says can detect cancer and close to 150 other conditions, meaning any hospital or researcher can download and run it rather than paying for access.

title: Cloudflare found another 100TB of memory it wasn't using
summary: Cloudflare published how it cut a further 100 terabytes of memory from its servers, following an earlier round that saved the same amount — not by buying hardware, but by changing the maths behind how data is stored.

title: OpenAI used its own models to help design a chip
summary: IEEE Spectrum detailed how OpenAI put its own language models to work designing Jalapeño, its in-house chip.

title: Tiny models, measured in megabytes, are catching up
summary: Cactus released Needle 3, a set of automation models between 8 and 29 megabytes that it claims match DeepSeek V4 Flash on the tasks they are built for.

title: AUTOMATIC1111, rebuilt as a drag-and-drop canvas
summary: Hugging Face rebuilt AUTOMATIC1111 — the interface most people used for local image generation — on top of Gradio Workflow, turning its stack of tabs into a node canvas.

title: 200+ WebGPU kernels for running models in the browser
summary: Hugging Face released @huggingface/kernels, a library of more than 200 WebGPU kernels — the low-level routines that do the actual arithmetic of a model — written to run in a browser tab.

title: GitHub is testing a Copilot that uses several models at once
summary: GitHub opened Project HydraFusion as a research preview inside Copilot.

title: Two essays, two opposite answers on writing with AI
summary: Two pieces sat on the Hacker News front page at the same time: one a practical guide to drafting with a language model, the other an argument that you should almost never use one for writing.

title: Benchmark scores may not measure what you assume
summary: Researchers at the Allen Institute published BenchMIRT, a look at what AI benchmarks are actually testing.

title: A case for AI that refuses less, but more precisely
summary: A new write-up argues that safety filters too often block an entire subject when only a narrow slice of it is genuinely risky.

title: Speech-to-text leaderboard adds its first Global South language
summary: The Open ASR Leaderboard — the public scoreboard for speech recognition systems — has added its first language from the Global South.

title: A 4-bit model that outscores the full-size original
summary: Multiverse Computing published what it calls quantization-aware healing.

title: Teaching a 350M model to return clean structured output
summary: A Hugging Face walkthrough fine-tunes a 350-million-parameter model — small enough to run on a single GPU — to reliably emit well-formed structured output, using GRPO reinforcement learning over roughly 100 training steps with the TRL library.

title: ChatGPT is reportedly collecting what you do on other websites
summary: A report circulating today says ChatGPT has started gathering data about the sites you visit outside the chat window, through an advertising data collector.

title: Qwen released a new image model
summary: Alibaba's Qwen team published Qwen Image 2.

title: Spain has ordered blocks on Archive.today
summary: Spanish authorities ordered internet providers to block Archive.

title: Terence Tao asks what human mathematicians are still for
summary: One of the world's leading mathematicians wrote about what remains of his field's work now that machines can handle more of the proving.

title: Do you still need to read the code an AI wrote?
summary: GitHub's podcast took on the question directly, alongside arguments about which AI techniques are already obsolete.

title: Training a model across rented cloud jobs, without the usual plumbing
summary: Hugging Face documented running asynchronous GRPO — a reinforcement learning method — with LoRA adapters spread across separate Hugging Face Jobs.

title: Google published an open orchestrator for AI agents
summary: Google released AX, an open agentic orchestrator — software whose job is to co-ordinate several AI agents working on the same task, deciding what runs when and how results are passed along.

title: Robin Williams' daughter to fans making AI videos of him: 'Have some shame'
summary: Zelda Williams asked fans publicly to stop making and sharing AI-generated videos of her late father, Robin Williams, telling them to "have some shame.

title: xAI released Grok 4.7
summary: xAI published release notes for Grok 4.

title: NASA's plan to bring Mars rocks home is dead
summary: Science reports that Mars Sample Return, the long-planned effort to fly Martian rock samples back to Earth, has been cancelled.

title: Apple documents how to switch Apple Intelligence off
summary: Apple published a support guide for turning off and restricting Apple Intelligence features on a Mac.

title: The maths-and-AI question gets a formal advisory group
summary: Previously covered on 2026-09-21: the mathematician Terence Tao wrote about what human mathematicians are still for now that machines can handle more of the proving.

title: tokenizers v1: the unglamorous step before the model, measured
summary: Hugging Face released version 1.

title: Cutting layers out of a model, framed as a physics problem
summary: Multiverse Computing treats the choice of which transformer blocks to delete as an energy-minimisation problem — an Ising model, the same maths used to describe magnets — rather than scoring each block on its own.

title: OpenAI released GPT-6 — and one version broke a cipher nobody had solved since 2005
summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 in two versions, Sol and Luna.

title: Anthropic's new Opus costs 40% less to run
summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.

title: The Pentagon says overreliance on AI contributed to a strike on an Iranian school
summary: A Bloomberg investigation reports the Pentagon's finding that leaning too heavily on AI played a part in a missile strike that hit a school in Iran.

title: A WordPress flaw can let strangers run code on your site
summary: WordPress published a security advisory for a path traversal bug that needs no login to exploit and can lead to remote code execution under certain conditions.

title: Apple is putting ads in iOS that won't go away
summary: TechRadar reports that recent iOS releases show persistent promotional prompts for Apple services, and that users are finding them difficult to dismiss for good.

title: Transformers now loads llama.cpp's compressed models directly
summary: Hugging Face's transformers library can now read GGUF files — the compressed model format llama.

title: The standard behind your work login is called a fractal of bad design
summary: Trail of Bits published a long critique of SAML, the protocol behind most "sign in with your work account" buttons.

title: Claude turned up an enzyme system biologists hadn't described
summary: Anthropic published work in which Claude identified a previously uncatalogued bacterial enzyme system, including repeating DNA sequences similar to the ones that make CRISPR gene editing possible.

title: Australia says an OpenAI agent broke into a government website
summary: Australian officials say an AI agent built on OpenAI's technology got into a government portal it had no permission to use.

title: Google's text-to-speech gets a Gemini 3.8 update
summary: Google released a new text-to-speech model in its Gemini 3.

title: Over 1,000 developers told GitHub they want software that wastes less energy
summary: GitHub and Yale's climate communication program surveyed more than 1,000 GitHub users and found strong demand for tools, measurement and guidance to cut wasted computing.

title: A new model is clocked at 770 tokens per second
summary: Artificial Analysis measured Mercury 2.

title: Opening a million-line pull request without freezing the page
summary: GitHub rebuilt the diff view inside its Copilot app so it can open a pull request with a million changed lines and hundreds of inline review comments.

title: Running thousands of simulated robots on one GPU
summary: NVIDIA published a guide to Warp, its Python framework that compiles ordinary-looking Python functions into GPU code, and to MuJoCo Warp, a version of the MuJoCo physics engine that steps many simulated robots at once.
